correctness.rationale: The ordered-pair color invariant is sufficient for the unlimited three-pebble game: after removing a pebble the two fixed pebbles determine the available two-color extensions, including equality moves. I independently reconstructed every support entry from Steiner-design counts. With v points, line size k, point degree r=(v−1)/(k−1), and b=vr/k lines, the degree of a line in the distinct-line meeting graph is d=k(r−1). For two distinct lines meeting in m∈{0,1} points, third points lie in both, either alone, or neither in counts m, k−m, k−m, v−2k+m. Third lines distinct from the pair meet both in u=k² if m=0 and u=(k−1)²+r−2 if m=1, by joining endpoints or passing through their common point. They meet just either specified line in d−m−u ways and neither in b−2−2(d−m)+u ways. The mixed and point-pair cases use the unique line on a pair of points; e.g. for p outside L, r−k lines through p miss L and b−1−d−(r−k) lines avoid both. The positivity patterns yield the six asserted tables. Exact replay checked every one of the 52 frozen signature rows and the projected atomic rank-two and rank-three types. In the high-dimensional all-field argument any two fixed objects lie in a three-space and all feasible patterns have witnesses there, including q=2. The plane counts need only the plane axioms. For E_n the disjoint-pair row first gains a line missing both at n=6; at n=4 its lines are exactly those of the affine plane of order two. Forgetting the meet/disjoint colors in the rank-three recursion merges D–F and leaves A, B, C distinct; rank two sees the same atomic two-element possibilities throughout. The stated four separators yield six distinct vectors: each line-pair subtest can bind the unused third name locally even when the matrix outside that subtest refers to all three line variables. This gives rank at most four. The representative minima are 6,14,10,15,21,21; AG(3,2) has 36 elements and PG(3,2) has 50, and higher-dimensional members are no smaller. Thus the uniform 21 bound is sharp.
